perf.summary: Hot loops recompute cell.Index and cell.Count separately (each a mask/shift of packedData) and frequently form (Index + Count); the two getters reload and re-mask the same word.
perf.currentCost: Loops like 'for (int i=(int)c.Index, ni=(int)(c.Index+c.Count); ...)' call Index twice and Count once, each performing a mask (Index) or shift+mask (Count) on packedData. Pattern repeats for every cell across Width*Height in Area/Region/Contour passes.
perf.proposedChange: Add an inlined helper 'public void GetSpanRange(out uint index, out uint count)' (or 'out int start, out int end') that reads packedData once and derives both fields, so callers do a single field load: 'cell.GetSpanRange(out uint start, out uint count); int ni = (int)(start+count);'. Mark Index/Count getters [MethodImpl(AggressiveInlining)] regardless.
perf.rationale: Reads packedData once instead of 2-3 times per cell and lets the JIT/Burst keep it in a register; removes a redundant masked load per loop header across O(Width*Height) iterations.
perf.risk: None to layout or semantics — purely a convenience accessor over the same bits; existing Index/Count remain. Caller refactors are mechanical. AggressiveInlining on trivial getters is safe.
